messages.subject: Hierarchical IRT using mirt
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to use a hierarchical IRT model using the mirt package. I am very new to this, so any help would be highly appreciated.   I have 4 items of polytomous in nature, say Item1, Item2, Item3 and Item 4. Each of these items have 8 different responses. My cluster is {Item1, Item2, Item 3} and {Item 4}. So the first 3 items are in one group and the last one is in 2nd group. How am I supposed to set up the model in mirt such that I can observe how the latent trait of these specified clusters are affecting each other. 

Right now I am using 

s <- 'F1 = 1,2,3
F2 = 4
COV = F1*F2'

model <- mirt.model(s)
mod1 <- mirt(data,model = model)

Is this the right approach? Any suggestion will be highly appreciated. 

Thanks
Souvik

messages.subject: Re: Hierarchical IRT using mirt
parts:
Thanks Phil for getting back. What I am trying to accomplish is that how the items are affecting each other. For example my 1st Item is Score in math and 2nd is score in engineering and 3rd item is developing software. I wish to see how the latent trait in math affect the latent trait in engineering. I have a longitudinal model, where my goal is to see how the latent trait in math over time affects the latent trait in engineering. The 3rd item is developing software. My goal in the next step is to see how the latent trait in math and engineering in combination affects the latent trait in developing software. My idea was to use multidimensional IRT to achieve this. If there is any other way, I shall be glad to learn about it. I highly appreciate any suggestion on this. 

Thanks
Souvik

parts: On Mon, Feb 29, 2016 at 4:44 PM, Souvik Bhattacharya <souvi...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks Phil for getting back. What I am trying to accomplish is that how the items are affecting each other. For example my 1st Item is Score in math and 2nd is score in engineering and 3rd item is developing software. I wish to see how the latent trait in math affect the latent trait in engineering. I have a longitudinal model, where my goal is to see how the latent trait in math over time affects the latent trait in engineering. The 3rd item is developing software. My goal in the next step is to see how the latent trait in math and engineering in combination affects the latent trait in developing software. My idea was to use multidimensional IRT to achieve this. If there is any other way, I shall be glad to learn about it. I highly appreciate any suggestion on this.

It sounds like you want to break this up into two separate analyses whereby you compute factor scores for the math-engineering factors separately, and fit a different model to obtain scores for the software. Following that, you'll want to use some type of regression function (accounting for the longitudinal effect, which someone complicates things because it depends on how these relationships evolve).

The reason I would say you should keep this separate is that you don't want the latent traits to affect each other at first since it sounds like you are more interested in predicting software dev from math and engineering (which could be a nonlinear relationship). If the relationship were linear you could probably use SEM to compute this type of model. 

Phil

Thanks
Souvik
